facts.claim: Fewer than 1 in 10 participants were able to recognize native advertising.
facts.quote: Although fewer than 1 in 10 participants were able to recognize native advertising, our study shows that effectively designed disclosure labels facilitate recognition.

facts.claim: Recognition of a natively formatted ad was triggered mostly by prior experience with social media ads, rather than ad disclosure.
facts.quote: Findings suggest that recognition of the natively formatted ad was triggered mostly by prior experience with social media ads, rather than ad disclosure.

facts.claim: A prominent disclosure enhances users’ perceived sponsorship transparency when the higher congruence makes it harder to discern a genuine endorsement from a sponsored one.
facts.quote: Moreover, a prominent disclosure enhances users’ perceived sponsorship transparency when the higher congruence makes it harder to discern a genuine endorsement from a sponsored one.

facts.claim: When the position of an ad on a news page is controlled for, a native ad generates a higher click-through rate because it better resembles the surrounding editorial content.
facts.quote: The results show that when the position of an ad on a news page is controlled for, a native ad generates a higher click-through rate because it better resembles the surrounding editorial content.

facts.claim: A display ad leads to more visual attention, brand recognition, and trustworthiness for the website than a native ad.
facts.quote: However, a display ad leads to more visual attention, brand recognition, and trustworthiness for the website than a native ad.

facts.claim: Middle or bottom positioning and wording using “advertising” or “sponsored” increased advertising recognition compared to other conditions.
facts.quote: Findings show that middle or bottom positioning and wording using “advertising” or “sponsored” increased advertising recognition compared to other conditions

research.angle: While many people fail to recognize native ads, recognition is often driven by prior experience with social media tactics rather than the presence of disclosures.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that native advertising is frequently difficult to recognize, but the effectiveness of disclosures varies significantly depending on their design, position, and the user's prior experience.
research.caveat: The research highlights that recognition is not solely dependent on disclosure, as factors like influencer-product fit and prior consumer knowledge also play significant roles.
